text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 13px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: C316 · Generation rate in the detector: where the light is absorbed, and the 40 µm length

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Book Sec. 7.5.1 (Figs 7.20, 7.21) · absorbed light makes electron–hole pairs ("generation"); mapping where it happens tells us how long to build the germanium detector

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: 1 · Where is the light absorbed? Side view of the detector (y along it, z = thickness)

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: end; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: illustrative toy model — not the book's 3D FDTD

text.style: font-size: 8.3px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: (a) log scale, full 50 µm: weak generation (with ripples) continues all along

text.style: font-size: 8.3px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: (b) linear scale, first 10 µm: the bright spot

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.3px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #64d2ff
font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #64d2ff
font-size: 7.8px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: colour = generation rate, normalised to its peak (bar: log scale of (a), 1 → 0.01). Ripples: light bounces between Ge and Si, and only the Ge absorbs.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: 2 · How long must the detector be?

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: end; fill: #a1a1a6
font-style: italic; font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: end; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: tuned to the book's 90% at 40 µm

g.text: Cumulative is normalised to the 50 µm model: 90% of what that model absorbs.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6
font-size: 8.3px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Length needed to absorb 90% of the light

text.style: font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Measured bars: our arithmetic, L = ln10 / α (Eq. 7.19),

text.style: font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: α fitted to Fig. 7.16 data (5.8 µm-wide devices).

text.style: font-size: 7.6px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: Book: the Ge model needs validation for thin films;

text.style: font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: "it appears that the Ge model underestimates the absorption".

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 9px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: Takeaway: most light is absorbed in the first several µm; the running total of generation says ≈ 40 µm catches ~90% — and real Ge may absorb faster.

text.style: font-size: 7.8px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Book Sec. 7.5.1 (pp. 276–277), Figs 7.20–7.21; Listing 7.2 thicknesses; Fig. 7.16 fit values. Heatmap and curves: illustrative toy model, not simulation data.
